The graph above shows the curve $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ and the line $y=-\sqrt{3}.$ Find the $x$-coordinate of the point $A.$

$$

$$
feedback.worked_solution:
The $y$-values of both functions are the same at the intersection point. Equating the two equations gives: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡x=-\sqrt{3}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\sqrt{3})=-\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

This value lies inside $-\frac{3\pi }{2}<x<0.$ Hence, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=-\frac{\pi }{3}.$ This is the $x$ coordinate of $B.$

To get another solution, we add $-\pi $ to the principal value. Thus,

$$
{x}_{2}=-\pi +x=-\pi -\frac{\pi }{3}=-\frac{4\pi }{3}.
$$

So, the $x$-coordinate of $A$ is $-\frac{4\pi }{3}.$
